doc.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29

title: Uniforms of the Piron and Tuxedo bands
summary: Cie Frazier describes Piron's checkered coats at Suburban Gardens in 1928 and subbing with the Original Tuxedo band.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: But now, Celestan and Pirone's band, you played with them. Yeah, them guys were uniform. What were they dressed like?

Well, Pirone band, before I went in that group, they was, I think, now they're uniformed, I don't know if they were tuxedos when they were working at Tranchino. But when I went in the band, would have been 30, let me see, no, 28. They was wearing, we was wearing, you know, what you call like a gamel of striped pants, and sort of a pants, sort of a checkered coat like. Like pep and salt coat, with gamel of striped pants when we were working at Suburban Garden nightclub. And then a tuxedo band, well they always used tuxedo suits. Well I played, you know, temporarily in Chinese plays sometimes with the original tuxedo band. When Chinese get high or something like that, he comes with me to go play with the band. And then lots of time I would go to China, that's in later years, but when they first had what that band organized I wouldn't know. But I know Chinese, my cousin John and Simon was playing, Paul Bones and all of them. Now one time they come got me to go play, it was called the All-A-Yong Club on St. Charles and Robert. And the other band, Blaks in the Way, chink down at these, got the kinfolks on my wife, Blaks in the Way, and I'm walking in with a set of drums, all the people look, I'm the main drummer of the band, think I'm late, you understand? And I just put it on all that, you see, release in cheek. But the Sunday didn't get mad, I just realized I was about an hour or something late, you know what I mean? First of all, I had no car to hustle the way to get up there. It happened that my brother come in there. But it has no car with it? No, St. Charles and Robert. Oh, yeah, yeah, man. A little more veering than it then. You got no drums, you got no car, man, so he got no car, man. No car, man. So he brought up to these little trucks. Street car, street car, you hear it? Yes, that's right. You have a pass, man. A drum permit, yeah. A drum and a bass, yeah. A drum permit, a good street car, that's true.
